title: Motivation, Person-Environment Fit, Hyperfocus, and Proposed Strengths in ADHD and Autism
background: This module evaluates motivational modulation, person-environment fit, hyperfocus, creativity, divergent thinking, and proposed neurodevelopmental strengths while actively testing nonspecific and selection-based explanations.
population: Adolescents and adults with ADHD, autism-spectrum disorder or traits, and relevant control groups.
intervention: Interest, novelty, reward, feedback, urgency, autonomy, person-environment fit, workplace or educational fit, hyperfocus, creativity, divergent thinking, or pattern recognition.
comparator: Low-interest or routine tasks, low-reward conditions, standardized environments, controls, or alternative explanatory variables.

outcomes_primary.name: Attention or task performance under different motivational conditions
Objective evidence for hyperfocus, creativity, divergent thinking, or pattern recognition

outcomes_secondary.name: Specificity, ecological validity, trade-offs, and confounding

inclusion: Adolescent or adult ADHD/autism sample or validated trait analysis.
Empirically examines motivation, task context, environmental fit, hyperfocus, creativity, divergent thinking, or pattern recognition.
Reports a comparative, within-person, or systematically synthesized result.
exclusion: Advocacy-only or conceptual claim without empirical outcome data.
No separable ADHD/autism group or validated trait analysis.
Purely pediatric educational study without developmental relevance.
No outcome relevant to claims H3, H6, or H10.

analysis.effect_measure: Narrative synthesis with construct-specific effect estimates where reported.

registration: Protocol frozen for AI-assisted rapid review on 2026-07-29; not prospectively registered.
disclaimer: AI Reviewer-1 rapid-review draft. Human Reviewer 2 and clinical sign-off remain pending. Not diagnostic or treatment guidance.
